title: A matrix library
description:
Build a small linear-algebra type that feels like a built-in one, using generics-free but trait-heavy Rust:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
struct Matrix { rows: usize, cols: usize, data: Vec<f64> }      // row-major

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum MatrixError { Empty, Ragged, Shape { left: (usize, usize), right: (usize, usize) }, NotSquare, Parse(String) }

impl Matrix {
    fn zeros(rows: usize, cols: usize) -> Matrix
    fn identity(n: usize) -> Matrix
    fn from_rows(rows: Vec<Vec<f64>>) -> Result<Matrix, MatrixError>    // Empty for no rows or empty rows; Ragged for uneven rows
    fn shape(&self) -> (usize, usize)
    fn transpose(&self) -> Matrix
    fn try_mul(&self, other: &Matrix) -> Result<Matrix, MatrixError>    // Shape error when cols != other.rows
    fn determinant(&self) -> Result<f64, MatrixError>                  // NotSquare for non-square matrices
}
```

and these trait implementations:

| Trait | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `Index<(usize, usize)>`, `IndexMut<(usize, usize)>` | `m[(r, c)]` reads and writes an element (panics outside the matrix) |
| `Add<&Matrix> for &Matrix`, `Sub<&Matrix> for &Matrix` | Element-wise; **panic** with a message containing `shape` when the shapes differ |
| `Mul<f64> for &Matrix` | Multiplies every element |
| `Mul<&Matrix> for &Matrix` | Matrix product; panics on a shape mismatch (use `try_mul` to get an error instead) |
| `Display` | Each row on its own line, elements separated by a space, with 2 decimals: `1.00 2.00\n3.00 4.00` (no newline at the end) |
| `FromStr` | Rows separated by `;`, numbers by white space: `"1 2; 3 4"`; parse errors become `MatrixError::Parse(<the bad text>)`, and an uneven shape `Ragged` |

The determinant can use cofactor expansion for small matrices or Gaussian elimination; the tests use matrices up to 4 × 4. Results only need to be correct to 1e-9.

starter.solution.rs:
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
struct Matrix {
    rows: usize,
    cols: usize,
    data: Vec<f64>,
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum MatrixError {
    Empty,
    Ragged,
    Shape { left: (usize, usize), right: (usize, usize) },
    NotSquare,
    Parse(String),
}

hints: Store the elements in one `Vec<f64>` in row-major order: element `(r, c)` is at `r * cols + c`. `Index` and `IndexMut` then make `m[(r, c)]` work everywhere, including inside your own methods.

`Index` and `IndexMut` live in `std::ops` like `Add` (lesson 4.03): `impl Index<(usize, usize)> for Matrix { type Output = f64; fn index(&self, (r, c): (usize, usize)) -> &f64 { &self.data[r * self.cols + c] } }` (the parameter pattern takes the tuple apart), and `impl IndexMut<(usize, usize)> for Matrix` adds `fn index_mut(&mut self, (r, c): (usize, usize)) -> &mut f64` returning `&mut self.data[...]`. `assert!` (lesson 3.05) gives the panic outside the matrix.
Implementing `Add<&Matrix> for &Matrix` (with `type Output = Matrix`) is what makes `&a + &b` compile without moving `a` or `b`.

For the determinant, Gaussian elimination is O(n³): pick the row with the largest value in the column as the pivot (swapping rows flips the sign), then subtract multiples of it from the rows below; the determinant is the product of the pivots.
requirements: Implement the operators for references (`&a + &b`) so that matrices are not moved by arithmetic.
Keep all fields private to a `mod linalg` and expose the type and the error with `pub use` or a path.
stretch: Make the type generic over the element type with a `Num` trait of your own, so `Matrix<i64>` and `Matrix<f64>` share the code.
